Tires are suspension. To enjoy the same ride and feel, a heavy rider/bike benefits from a wider tire than a lighter rider/bike.

Instead of starting with a tire size, tell us how you ride. Based on your input, we'll recommend a Rene Herse tire for your weight and riding style, then calculate your recommended pressure.

Before you choose a tire, work out how wide a tire your frame will take. Measure the tightest gap between your current tire and the frame or fork — usually at the chainstays or the fork crown — and we'll work out the widest tire that will still clear.

Not sure about your clearances and current tire width? Click here for instructions how to measure.

  • This leaves 4 mm of clearance on each side, the ISO standard — enough for mud, a slightly out-of-true wheel and a tire growing as it wears in.
  • It is a guide, not a guarantee: frames vary, and a tire's width depends on the rim it is mounted on. Check the clearance yourself before riding a new tire in anger.
